choices.pr_choice: Golfs the proofs of eight declarations across seven files in unrelated areas (finsets, rationals, product measures, portmanteau, limsup, disintegration, metric balls) as one batched PR.
choices.excerpt: * Up to ~5 changed files per PR
choices.status_reason: The goal is to golf these particular proofs; the change modifies exactly these declarations.
choices.visibility_reason: The task cannot be stated without naming the proofs to golf; the files are also in the packet.
choices.consequence: Seven files in unrelated areas exceed the stated ~5-file guideline and need reviewers from several areas; a split would change review routing, not users.

choices.pr_choice: Changes only proof bodies: every name, statement, attribute, docstring and comment stays, and no declaration or import is added.
choices.status_reason: Kind 'proof changes only', decided from the change, which alters no statement.
choices.visibility_reason: Without it the brief would read as an invitation to restate or redesign the results.
choices.consequence: Changing a statement or attribute would break downstream uses such as Rat.inv_natCast_den_of_pos and change simp behaviour of Finset.mem_map_equiv.

choices.pr_choice: Keeps the metric-ball lemma as its own theorem even though its new proof is a single application of a general order lemma, rather than making it an alias or deprecating it.
choices.status_reason: Kind 'proof changes only': the statement and name must keep working.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief keeps every changed declaration's name and statement; that it now reduces to a general existing lemma stays hidden.
choices.consequence: An alias or deprecation would shrink the API; keeping it preserves the metric-specific name and its docstring cross-reference for users.

choices.pr_choice: Closes two proofs with grind after a simp only normalisation, accepting the slower elaboration the description reports for both.
choices.consequence: Both proofs got slower (<10 ms to 25 ms and 17 ms); a grind proof depends on grind's evolving behaviour and annotations, while a structured or simp-only proof would stay fast and more predictable.

choices.pr_choice: Normalises with mem_map and Equiv.coe_toEmbedding before the closing automation, replacing the explicit two-direction term proof.
Rewrites with den_inv and num_intCast instead of unfolding the cast through divInt and proving coprimality by hand.
Finishes with simp only [pi_pi, this] and Fintype.prod_equiv with a pointwise congrFun rfl, replacing Finset.prod_equiv and a manual congr on e.apply_symm_apply.

Derives the real-valued primed lemma from the unprimed portmanteau lemma after rewriting the hypothesis with ProbabilityMeasure.measureReal_eq_coe_coeFn and NNReal.toReal_limsup, dropping the ENNReal route and the case split on the trivial filter.
choices.consequence: Changes which portmanteau variant this lemma depends on (the NNReal-valued one rather than the ENNReal one), coupling it to that statement and to NNReal.toReal_limsup; the description reports 268 ms to <10 ms.

choices.pr_choice: Turns the goal into a finite conjunction of eventually-statements with sup'_lt_iff and eventually_all_finset and applies eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt pointwise, replacing the explicit intersection witness.
choices.excerpt: +    simp only [gt_iff_lt, sup'_lt_iff, eventually_all_finset] at hb ⊢

choices.pr_choice: In both versions, closes with the existing product-set lemma (Kernel.compProd_apply_prod / compProd_apply_prod) after simp only [this], replacing the indicator-function argument and the classical block.
Gives a term-mode proof by exists_between', relying on ball membership unfolding definitionally to a distance inequality, instead of an explicit midpoint with linarith after simp only [mem_ball].
choices.consequence: The term proof relies on the definitional unfolding of Metric.ball membership; the old proof went through mem_ball and would survive a change to that definition.

choices.pr_choice: Rewrites only the closing part of four proofs, keeping their existing let/have setup steps unchanged.
Edits each proof in place in its existing file.
choices.status_reason: Proof changes to existing declarations happen where those declarations live.

feasibility_reason: The task is to shorten eight named proofs without changing their statements; that can be stated fully while every proof route (the closing automation, the lemmas reused, the term-mode proof, the new dependency of the portmanteau lemma, the partial rewrites) stays hidden. Only the set of declarations and the preservation of their statements are exposed, and both define the task.
brief_omits: The tactic names in the title and the per-declaration timing numbers in the description, because both reveal the proof route (the two proofs that got slower are the ones closed by automation); the description's exact batch-size limits (only that it is a size-limited series is said); that four proofs were rewritten only in part; that one statement now reduces to a general existing lemma.
